failure_anatomy.root_cause: crawler.A_RE = "([^<]*)" requires href immediately after '...; the intermediate class attribute makes them invisible to the parser. Nav/contextual/TOC anchors (no attributes) were parsed, so the crawl ran on a 12-page deterministic graph without the stochastic region.
failure_anatomy.why_pilots_missed_it: Pre-freeze pilots verified determinism, page coverage, title stability and estimator mechanics, but did not assert nonzero stub-click mass. power_sim.page_links included sA/sB abstractly, so simulated-power validation covered the estimators but not the live parse loop - a sim/live mismatch.
failure_anatomy.minimal_future_fix_candidate_NOT_APPLIED: Parser must match anchors with arbitrary attributes (e.g., <a\b[^>]*href='...'>) and any future prereg must add a sampling-coverage gate (nonzero expected-and-observed mass on every action class of interest) verified pre-outcome.

seal_decoding.reason: Arm identity carries zero information about byte-identical void datasets; decoding would be pure theater. The sealed mapping remains committed and digest-attested for independent audit.

negative_knowledge: A served-DOM regex parser that assumes attribute-free anchors silently reduces a stochastic Web fixture to its deterministic skeleton; arm-level effects then vanish identically rather than noisily, which is detectable ONLY by an explicit action-class coverage check.
Simulator-based power validation does not exercise the live parse loop; sim/live parity checks must include realized action-class distributions.
Byte-identical multi-arm datasets are a red-flag signature of sampler degeneracy, not of matched controls.
